neighbours.label: vocabulary of social or intellectual marginality: fringe(s), margins, periphery, liminal, 'the cracks' (literal outskirts and edges stay quiet)
fire: Such theories were long dismissed as the fringe of serious economics.
Poor families often live on the margins of city life.
Her paintings sat at the periphery of the art world for years.
He jotted little reminders in the margins of his textbook.
Extremist views moved from the fringes into parliament.
The novel explores a liminal moment between childhood and adulthood.
Too many veterans fall through the cracks of the welfare system.
A few fringe candidates also stood in the election.
quiet: Such theories were long accepted as the core of serious economics.
Poor families often live on the outskirts of the city.
Her paintings sat at the heart of the art world for years.
He jotted little reminders on the first page of his textbook.
Extremist views moved from the street into parliament.
The novel explores a quiet moment between childhood and adulthood.
Too many veterans depend on the support of the welfare system.
A few independent candidates also stood in the election.

notes: Probes: fringe 0.57, margins 0.62-0.67, cracks 0.43, Liminal 0.81, periphery 0.36; outskirts 0.07, sidelines 0.06, edge 0.08, middle 0.02. Word-shaped: not the general idea of an edge.
